Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{2}{5},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{2}{5}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{2}{5} & =\frac{2x+4}{6x+8} \\ 2(6x+8) & =5(2x+4) \\ 12x+16 & =10x+20 \\ 12x-10x & =20-16 \\ 2x & =4 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x+4=2(2)+4=8, \\ AC & =6x+8=6(2)+8=20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 20\cdot 8 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$
